title: Unlimited: No Player Limit
description:
Play [b]Slay the Spire 2[/b] multiplayer with up to 16 players.

The vanilla game caps lobbies at 4; this mod raises the cap to 16 and lets you configure it from the in-game settings menu.

[h2]Features[/h2]
[list]
[*]Set max players from 2 to 16 via the in-game Settings menu
[*]Changes save automatically
[*]Supports both Steam lobbies and direct IP (ENet) connections
[*]Scales enemy difficulty to match your player count
[*]Optional: override the player count used for difficulty scaling (1–16), independent of how many are actually connected — including an optional toggle to apply it in singleplayer as a challenge mode
[*]Lightweight: Harmony patches only — no game file modifications
[/list]

[b]All players in the lobby must have the mod installed.[/b]

[h2]Recommended Mods[/h2]
[url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3747532120]Vanilla and Modded Saves Merger[/url] — unifies your save directory so modded and vanilla play share the same progression.

[h2]Configuration[/h2]
Open [b]Settings[/b] in-game and use the [b]Max Players[/b] slider (range: 2–16). Changes save automatically. The default is 8 players.

16 is a hard limit, not a slider preference: the mod widens the lobby packet's player-list header to a fixed width sized for 16 players so that every peer agrees on the wire format. Forcing a higher number through the config file is not supported and will break lobbies.

If you want to set the count without launching the game, edit [i]sts2unlimited.maxplayers.txt[/i] next to the mod's files and restart. Note this is a legacy fallback: once you have used the in-game slider the value lives in [i]sts2unlimited.settings.json[/i] and the text file is ignored.
changeNote:
v1.0.1: Fixes the in-game Settings menu cutting off the bottom of the General page. The mod's own Max Players and difficulty options sit at the end of that page, and the last rows could not be scrolled to — with several mods adding options there, a good part of the page became unreachable.

The settings panel works out its scroll height when it is created, which happens before any mod has added its rows, and after that only when the window is resized — which is why toggling fullscreen temporarily brought the missing rows back. It now re-measures whenever the contents of the page change, so it also keeps up when the difficulty rows are shown or hidden by their toggle, and when other mods add rows of their own.

No gameplay or multiplayer changes in this release; v1.0.0's lobby-join fix still applies, so hosts should be on v1.0.0 or later.
